ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “Bodhi originally has no tree” is Huineng’s first verse line, preserved as a quoted case-line and repeatedly appraised in later encounters.
EvidenceBody: Two transmissions explicitly assign the line to Huineng and preserve it with the mirror, nothing-at-all, and dust lines.
Daguan Tanying raises both Shenxiu’s and Huineng’s verses, then refuses to treat either as a final possession; Yulin Tongxiu reuses Huineng’s line as an answer to “the phrase without.”
The entry therefore preserves an attributed, repeatable case-line. It does not turn the line into a free-standing definition of bodhi or decide the patriarchs’ appraisals.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A line from Huineng’s verse becomes portable encounter material that later masters quote, compare, criticize, and give as an answer.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The records themselves place the line under appraisal; the dictionary does not equate reciting it with seeing one’s nature.
